pdm-acid-base: What three things does an arterial blood gas assess?
Oxygenation, ventilation and acid-base status
Which values evaluate acid-base status on the blood gas?
pH, bicarbonate and carbon dioxide
Which blood gas value assesses ventilation?
The partial pressure of carbon dioxide
What does the carbon dioxide pressure indicate about breathing?
The rate and depth of respirations
What is the major chemical factor regulating ventilation?
Carbon dioxide in the blood and cerebrospinal fluid
As carbon dioxide rises, what happens to ventilation?
It increases
What does the partial pressure of oxygen measure?
Oxygen dissolved in plasma
What share of blood oxygen is dissolved in plasma?
Less than 2%
What share of blood oxygen is bound to hemoglobin?
What directly affects the oxygen pressure?
The fraction of inspired oxygen
What is the fraction of inspired oxygen?
The amount of oxygen in the air taken into the lungs
Which value assesses the efficacy of oxygen therapy?
The partial pressure of oxygen
What does the oxygen saturation express?
The ratio of hemoglobin's actual oxygen to its maximum capacity
Does saturation show the oxygen content?
No: the relationship between oxygen and hemoglobin
Besides the blood gas, what measures oxygen saturation?
Pulse oximetry
What is the oxygen content?
The actual amount of oxygen in the blood
What is the oxygen capacity?
The maximum oxygen that can combine with hemoglobin
When does carboxyhemoglobin form?
When hemoglobin is exposed to carbon monoxide
How much greater is hemoglobin's affinity for carbon monoxide than for oxygen?
240 times
What does the carboxyhemoglobin result indicate?
The amount of carbon monoxide poisoning
What is another name for base excess?
Whole blood buffer base
What share of the buffer base is bicarbonate?
Half
Which anions make up the other half of the buffer base?
Plasma proteins and phosphates
What is base excess critically important for?
Telling respiratory from nonrespiratory change
What does a negative base excess indicate?
A base deficit (nonvolatile acid excess)
What does a positive base excess indicate?
A base excess (nonvolatile acid deficit)
Which acid is the volatile acid?
Carbonic acid
Name the nonvolatile acids.
Dietary acids, lactic acids, ketoacids
Where does oxygen bind hemoglobin on the curve?
High oxygen pressure: the pulmonary capillaries
Where is oxygen released on the curve?
Low oxygen pressure: the tissue capillaries
Which way does alkalosis shift the curve?
Left: oxygen bonds more tightly
Which way does acidosis shift the curve?
Right: oxygen released more easily
Name the four right-shift causes.
More hydrogen ions, carbon dioxide, temperature and BPG (2,3-bisphosphoglycerate)
Why is arterial blood sampled?
It is a better mixture of blood
What can alter a venous sample?
Temperature, perfusion, movement, local infection
Does the blood gas show the degree of an abnormality?
No: assess the patient
Besides lung oxygenation, what does arterial blood indicate?
Whether the heart and circulation are failing
Is venous carbon dioxide higher or lower than arterial?
Higher (41 to 57 mm Hg)
Is venous pH higher or lower than arterial?
Lower (7.31 to 7.41)
Which artery is usually the sampling site?
The radial artery
What does the Allen test check?
Collateral supply via the ulnar and radial arteries
No collateral circulation: what next?
Choose another site
Which other arteries can be sampled?
Femoral and brachial
What three features make an artery suitable?
Collateral flow, superficial and accessible, non-sensitive tissue
What syringe collects the sample?
A pre-heparinized self-filling syringe
What happens to the sample before it goes to the lab?
Air bubbles removed, placed on ice
What must be noted with every sample?
Room air or the supplemental oxygen
How old can a blood gas sample be?
Less than 3 hours
How long is pressure held after an arterial stick?
At least 2 minutes, until bleeding stops
Name the six indications for an arterial blood gas.
Oxygenation, ventilation, acid-base status, therapy response, critically ill, pre/post-operative baseline
Acidosis is a pH below what?
Alkalosis is a pH above what?
Which organs primarily buffer acid-base balance?
The lungs and the kidneys
What is the first step in reading a blood gas?
The pH
What is the last step of the step-wise approach?
Do the labs fit the clinical presentation?
High carbon dioxide usually means what?
Retention from hypoventilation
Low carbon dioxide usually means what?
Hyperventilation
Name the causes of a low carbon dioxide.
Hypoxia, pulmonary emboli, anxiety, pain (and pregnancy)
How do narcotics raise the carbon dioxide?
They impair the respiratory center
Name two causes of a high oxygen pressure.
Increased inspired oxygen, hyperventilation
How do the kidneys compensate a respiratory disorder?
By adjusting bicarbonate reabsorption, over days
How is a metabolic disorder compensated?
By adjusting ventilation and carbon dioxide, over minutes to hours
Compensation for metabolic acidosis?
Carbon dioxide decreases
Compensation for metabolic alkalosis?
Carbon dioxide increases
Compensation for respiratory acidosis?
Bicarbonate increases
Compensation for respiratory alkalosis?
Bicarbonate decreases
Acute respiratory acidosis findings?
pH low, carbon dioxide high, bicarbonate normal
Which drugs cause acute respiratory acidosis?
Opioids, barbiturates, anesthetics
Chronic respiratory acidosis: what happens to bicarbonate?
It rises (metabolic compensation)
Kyphoscoliosis causes respiratory acidosis through what?
Chest wall dysfunction
Respiratory alkalosis findings?
pH high, carbon dioxide low, bicarbonate normal
Fever causes respiratory alkalosis how?
Stimulating the brainstem respiratory center
Salicylates and sepsis may cause which mixed picture?
Respiratory alkalosis plus metabolic acidosis
Severe heart failure leads to which acid-base disorder?
Metabolic acidosis (hypoperfusion, lactic acidosis)
Metabolic acidosis findings?
pH low, carbon dioxide normal, bicarbonate decreased
Name the acid-gain causes of metabolic acidosis.
Renal failure, diabetic ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, anaerobic metabolism
Name the base-loss causes of metabolic acidosis.
Diarrhea, renal tubular acidosis
Metabolic alkalosis findings?
pH high, carbon dioxide normal, bicarbonate increased
Name the causes of metabolic alkalosis.
Bicarbonate given, vomiting or nasogastric suction, potassium or chloride depletion
In acidosis, where does potassium go?
Out of the cells: hyperkalemia
In alkalosis, where does potassium go?
Into the cells: hypokalemia
What is the anion gap formula?
Sodium minus (chloride plus bicarbonate)
What is the normal anion gap?
9 to 15
Which anion makes up most of the normal gap?
Serum albumin
An elevated gap is usually due to what?
More unmeasured anions
Less often, an elevated gap is due to what?
Fewer unmeasured cations
A decreased gap is usually due to what?
More unmeasured cations (lithium)
Which lab problem lowers the gap in hyperlipidemia?
Skewed sodium and chloride estimates
How is the gap corrected for low albumin?
Add 2.5 for each 1 g/dL below 4.5
